newsitem.title: USA: Long Distance sees Q2 loss $.10/sh or less.
newsitem.headline: Long Distance sees Q2 loss $.10/sh or less.

text.p: Long Distance Direct Holdings Inc said Thursday it expects a second-quarter loss of no more than $0.10 per share fully diluted on revenues of about $2.7 million.

The company also said it expects third quarter loss to be lower than the second quarter loss on increased revenues, and it expects to become profitable on a higher revenue base by the end of the year.
The company said it expects investment and expense related to the broadening of its infrastructure to continue into the third quarter.
The company reported a loss for the second quarter of fiscal 1996 of $244,000, or $0.06 per share, on 5.1 million shares outstanding.
The company's revenues were $1.7 million for the second quarter of 1996, and $2.1 million for the first quarter of 1997.
The company's expected loss per share for the second quarter is on a share base of 11.3 million.
The company said its customer base increased more than 100 percent from 12,000 net customers in January 1997 to 24,000 today. It expects that rate of growth to continue.
